Subject: Recap & pilot sizing: Tactica discovery — latency/throughput SLOs

Hi Elena — thanks again for the sync today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same record.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: production latency spikes during peak web-search traffic (user-facing query suggestions).
- Target SLOs: p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms, steady-state TPS ~120 req/s, burst to 300 req/s for 10–15s windows.
- Model: currently experimenting with a finetuned 8B transformer (in-house) — willing to test a 8B/13B quantized variant.
- Deployment preference: private VPC Dedicated trial, with Hosted fallback for edge bursts.

What we heard today (my notes):
- Production traffic is highly spiky with diurnal peaks and sudden marketing-driven bursts. Key requirement is predictable p95 latency for the autosuggest API.
- Cost sensitivity for steady-state; they want unit economics visibility (tokens/second cost) for different quantization profiles.
- Need SOC2 evidence and audit log retention for compliance (we discussed Private offering).

Proposed pilot (next steps):
1) Pilot window: 2 weeks (staging -> small production traffic split)
2) Topology: Dedicated pool (4x A100e-equivalent GPUs) + 1x hot-hosted fallback region for burst routing. KV cache enabled on prefix-heavy endpoints.
3) Initial sizing: aim for 120 req/s sustained with 2x buffer for spikes; we recommend starting with 8x GPU equivalent for safe headroom. See attached "proposed-pilot-sizing.xlsx" for a quick estimate.
4) Technical deep-dive: schedule a 60-minute runbook call to confirm tokenization, max-seq lengths, batching constraints and exact model artifacts.

Please confirm (a) the model artifact you want us to use for the pilot (docker/artifact link or HF model id), (b) an initial list of test prompts for quality regression checks, and (c) whether you can share sample traffic (anonymized) or at least sequence length distributions.

Attachments: tactica-painpoints-onepager.pdf, proposed-pilot-sizing.xlsx

Thanks — I can book the technical call for this week if that works.

—Sean

Elena — perfect, thank you. Quick answers inline and a couple of proposed guardrails for the technical call: 

On quantization:
- Dedicated runtime supports int8 and lower-bit quantization paths (4-bit experiments) — results vary by model and token distribution. For short, suggestion-like prompts (median 48 tokens) we generally see negligible quality drop for int8; 4-bit can be good but requires evals on your prompt set. We'll bring quantization profiles and comparison plots to the deep-dive.

On batching / mixed lengths:
- Runtime uses dynamic bucketing + continuous batching. For p95-sensitive endpoints we recommend: max_batch_latency = 8ms, prioritized routing (small-batch fast-path) for frontend-synchronous calls, and prefix KV cache for high-reuse prefixes. That will limit latency impact from long-seq requests.

Proposed pilot sizing (refined):
- Staging split: 5% traffic -> Dedicated pool (4 GPUs to start), monitor p95. If p95 >= 150ms at 5% -> scale to 8 GPUs.
- Burst plan: hot-hosted fallback in region us-west to absorb bursts; we can set policy to route bursts >200 req/s to hosted variant with a model downgrade (13B quantized) if needed.

Action items before the technical call:
- Jose: model OCI registry link + HF fallback id.
- Elena: anonymized trace (seq length histogram) — thanks for offering that.
- Camila / Karthik / Laura: I'll leave the ops & security asks to you two (SOC2 retention Qs and VPC peering checklist).

I'll suggest the following slots for the deep-dive (60m): Wed 12/15 09:00-10:00 PT or Wed 12/15 13:00-14:00 PT. Which works best?

Cheers,
—Sean
